result:
I fixed all five problems. The typecheck and the full test suite (617 tests) pass. A throwaway check with 60 workspaces, one of them deleted, also passed: the overdue alerts reached all 59 live workspaces, none reached the deleted one, and three recount runs covered all 59. I removed that check afterwards.

**Cause:** the overdue alerts, the daily digest and the retention cleanup all got their workspaces from the usage recount's list. That list was capped at 25–50 workspaces and put the most recently measured ones first. It also still included deleted workspaces. On top of that, every small counter adjustment updated the "measured at" time, so busy workspaces kept moving to the front. That is why the recount kept picking the same ones and the others' counters kept drifting.

**Changes:**
- **Overdue alerts, digest and retention cleanup** now go through every workspace that hasn't been deleted, a page at a time. The new helper is in `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`. What each job does for a single workspace is unchanged: an overdue issue is still announced once, and the digest still marks notifications as read so it isn't sent twice.
- **Usage recount** (`src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts`):
  - It picks up to 25 workspaces, ordered by how long ago they were last recounted. Workspaces that have never been recounted come first, and deleted workspaces are skipped.
  - Small counter adjustments no longer change the "measured at" time, so they don't move a workspace in the queue.
  - A blank counter row created on first read counts as "never recounted", so that workspace is recounted early.
  - A recount always stamps a time later than any earlier recount, so the workspace goes to the back of the queue even when several recounts happen in the same millisecond.

**One side effect:** to keep recounted workspaces strictly in order, a recount's timestamp can land a millisecond or so after the actual time. "Measured at" now also means "last recounted", not "last changed". Nothing in the UI shows this field today.
